sources.locator: "Tunisian campaign", revision 1375742094: "withdrawn into and occupied Tunisia, after their defeat in the Western Desert and the success of Operation Torch"

explanation: “Tunisian campaign”, at revision 1375742094, lead: “Despite initial successes by the German and Italian forces brought from the mainland and which had withdrawn into and occupied Tunisia, after their defeat in the Western Desert and the success of Operation Torch, massive supply interdiction efforts and Allied assaults from east and west led to the decisive defeat of the Axis.” The same article’s § Operation Torch says what the landings were for: “On 8 November, Operation Torch landed Allied forces in Algeria (at Oran and Algiers) and Morocco (at Casablanca) with the intention that once Vichy forces in Algeria had capitulated, an advance would be made to Tunis.” The campaign began nine days after the landings and the article names Torch as one of the two things that drove the Axis into Tunisia and brought the Allies at them from the west. `caused`: the article does not say Torch made the campaign possible, it says the campaign is what Torch ran into. **The other cause the sentence names, the defeat in the Western Desert, is not a record this atlas holds** — `Q625798`, the Western Desert campaign — and when it is written this edge should be read beside a second one from it. `probable`, not `consensus`: A2 allows `consensus` only through a work Wikipedia cites, and rule 22 would refuse it on a Wikipedia citation anyway.
